text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Did the infant pass any stool at all in the first 48 hours of life, or has there been absolutely no meconium passage? Also, during the physical exam, I am going to perform a digital rectal examination to check for the presence of stool and anal tone.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Inability to pass meconium, Abdominal distension.

speaker: Doctor
text: The digital rectal exam revealed a tight, high-pressure anal sphincter with an empty rectum, and upon withdrawal, there was a significant explosive expulsion of stool and gas. This "blast" of stool is highly characteristic of Hirschsprung disease. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray
